Andrew Wilkening, Josh Henderson, Mitch Deason, Tanio Klyce
fields.machine_toys:
Pokémon-catching and collection system spanning four distinct habitats.
Persistent Pokémon collection through Stern Insider Connected, allowing players to retain captured Pokémon across compatible machines.
Four primary playable Pokémon: Pikachu, Bulbasaur, Squirtle, and Charmander, each with individual story modes and training mechanics.
Pokémon Rival Battles featuring different opponents, attack behaviors, and strategic character selection.
Interactive Team Rocket Meowth Balloon mechanism that descends into the battle arena during gameplay.
Pokédex captive-ball mechanism used to scan Pokémon and earn gameplay assists.
Poké Ball assembly used during Pokémon-catching sequences, with an animated ball-lock mechanism on Premium and Limited Edition models.
Animatronic Pikachu with synchronized movement and custom voice recordings on Premium and Limited Edition models.
Squirtle Whirlpool bowl mechanism on Premium and Limited Edition models.
Psyduck Sneak-In scoop on Premium and Limited Edition models, replaced by a stationary target on the Pro.
Interactive battle arena electromagnet on Premium and Limited Edition models.
Multiple Team Rocket and character-specific multiball modes.
Shot multipliers, Pokémon training, timed story modes, and progressive mini-wizard modes.
Footage from the original Pokémon animated television series.
Custom recorded speech for Pikachu and Team Rocket leader Giovanni.
Original Pokémon animated-series theme song.
Stern SPIKE 3 electronics platform.
Optional interactive Magikarp topper featuring an exclusive multiball mode.
Limited Edition production of 750 numbered machines, featuring upgraded cabinet lighting, mirrored backglass, enhanced audio, anti-reflection playfield glass, and factory-installed shaker motor.
fields.machine_comments:
Pokémon was Stern Pinball's first original cornerstone title of 2026, released during the Pokémon franchise's 30th anniversary year.
Pokémon was originally introduced in Japan in February 1996 with the release of Pokémon Red and Green for the Nintendo Game Boy.
The game was co-designed by George Gomez and Jack Danger, bringing together two Stern designers with notably different backgrounds and approaches to pinball design.
Unlike most modern Stern titles, the cabinet, backbox, translite, and playfield artwork were created primarily by The Pokémon Company International's internal art team rather than Stern's usual commissioned pinball artists.
The game draws heavily from the original Pokémon animated series rather than focusing exclusively on the franchise's video games or trading card game.
Stern incorporated footage from the original animated television series, along with the original Pokémon theme song and custom character recordings.
Pokémon marked Nintendo's return to licensed, commercially manufactured physical pinball machines after more than three decades.
Pokémon was announced on February 12, 2026, with the public reveal and commercial launch taking place during the franchise's anniversary year.
The game's launch was reportedly delayed by the extensive artwork and content approval process required by The Pokémon Company International.
Stern's design team confirmed that the 2026 release was intended to serve as the franchise's 30th anniversary pinball title, rather than being followed by a separately themed anniversary edition.
The game's persistent Pokémon collection was designed around Stern Insider Connected, allowing captured Pokémon to remain associated with a player's account between games and locations.
The Premium and Limited Edition models share the same primary playfield mechanisms, while the Limited Edition adds upgraded cabinet presentation, lighting, audio, and collector-oriented features.
The Limited Edition was restricted to 750 individually numbered machines worldwide.
The official Magikarp topper was released with its own exclusive multiball mode, making it a gameplay-expanding accessory rather than a purely decorative topper.
The Magikarp topper's letter-collection feature allows progress toward its exclusive multiball to persist between games and players.
fields.machine_ornament: Stern released an officially licensed Magikarp topper for Pokémon in June 2026, compatible with the Pro, Premium, and Limited Edition models. The topper features a mechanically animated Magikarp emerging from an ocean scene, moving wave mechanisms, synch
fields.machine_videomode: The game's LCD display features animated Pokémon battles, Pokémon-catching sequences, original television-series footage, and other interactive presentations that accompany physical pinball gameplay. These sequences are integrated into the game's rules and do not constitute a separate video mode controlled independently of the pinball.

Update instructions - Games connected to Stern Insider Connected:
1 - Open the coin door and press the black/enter button to enter Test Mode.
2 - Using the 4 buttons on the coin door, navigate to the Stern Insider Connected Setup menu.
3 - Using the 4 buttons on the coin door, navigate down to the Software Update menu.
4 - If a software update is available, this page will give you the option to
    download and install it manually.  From this menu you can also select to install these
    updates automatically.

Update instructions - All Games:
1 - Download the zip file
2 - Unzip the file, this will create a folder that contains SPK file(s).
3 - Open the folder, copy the file(s) to the root level of a FAT32 formatted
    USB stick.  (Do not copy the folder.)
4 - Power game off
5 - Insert USB stick
6 - Turn on game
7 - After game boots up it will give the option for software update
8 - Volume buttons change options for full or quick update. Enter selects the
    option and starts the update.
9 - Once update is completed game will prompt user to power game off and
    remove USB stick.

V.87 - 10/29/2026
=======================
==NEW==
 - Story Mode Multiplier
   - Catching a Pokémon increases the Story Mode Multiplier by +1X 
     for the next Story Mode, up to a max of 3X.
 - Team Rocket Multiball multiplier
   - Winning a Rival Battle increases the Team Rocket Multiplier by +1X
     for the rest of the game, up to a max of 3X.
   - If the Team Rocket Multiplier is already 3X, then winning a Rival Battle
     will increase the Victory Bonus by 10 million for the first time and 
     by 15 million for subsequent victories.
 - Pokédex scan timer speed-up
   - When a Pokémon appears, Trainers can speed-up the Pokédex scan timer by
     holding the action button.
 - Added DJ Mixer to the Game Mode Menu.
 - Added Pokémon Collection Viewer to the Game Mode Menu. 
   Trainers can login to view the Pokémon they have collected on the machine.
 - Added Achievements pages to Instant Info.
 - Added Pokémon tutorial videos to Attract Mode.
 - Added High Score To Date screens for the Tier 2 Story Modes.
 - Added three additional variations of 5-shot CATCH sequences.

==TWEAKS==
 - The first Team Rocket Multiball is started by hitting the Meowth Balloon instead of the center shot.
 - Training Targets - hitting a lit Training target will spot an unlit neighbor target.
 - Progress towards Discovering Pokémon is carried over between Story Modes and Rival Battles.
 - Maximum number of Pokémon catches needed to light Battle reduced from 3 to 2.

==FIXED==
 - The Squirtle Team Feature award video would keep looping until a higher priority
   award video was played.

==SYSTEM 4.40==
 -  Updated the graphical Service Menu->Diagnostics->LED Test:
     The test now does RGB separately when single stepping, and W when holding the up or down button.
     Removed obsolete adjustment which selected lamp test grouping (RGB separately or W).
     Added RGB LED Test to the LED Test menu.
 - Updated to nodeboard firmware/protocol v1.41.0
 - Various behind the scenes improvements for correctness and performance.

V.86 - 9/15/2026
=======================

==NEW==
 - Insider Connected
   - View Pokémon Collection in the Stern Insider Connected App
   - Earn Insider Connected Achievements
   - Unlock Travel at Game Start: Log in with Insider Connected and play 
     the Forest Battle to unlock the ability to travel to other biomes
     at the start of the game. 
 - Added 31 Pokémon
 - Pikachu vs Mimikyu
   - Play "Pikachu vs Raichu" and then shoot the right ramp to advance and start 
     "Pikachu vs Mimikyu" multiball.
   - Hit battle targets (purple) to score Mimikyu awards and light Pikachu jackpots (yellow).
   - Hit Pikachu jackpots to light the super jackpot at the center lane (purple/yellow).
 - Bulbasaur 2
   - Play "Bulbasaur 1" and then shoot the left orbit to advance and start "Bulbasaur 2".
   - Use the flipper buttons to move the green and purple shot arrows.
   - Overlap the green and purple shot arrows for triple awards.
   - Shoot 3 triple awards to light the Pokédex captive ball to complete the mode.
 - Squirtle 2
   - Play "Squirtle 1" and then shoot the left ramp to advance and start "Squirtle 2".
   - 5 shots are "on fire" (red/orange flickering).
   - Shoot a shot once so that the fire is "going out" (blue flickering). 
   - Shoot shots that are "going out" to put out the fire. This award is multiplied by
     the number of shots that are "going out".
   - When all shots are put out, shoot the captive ball to complete the mode.
 - Charmander 2
   - Play "Charmander 1" and then shoot the right orbit to advance and start "Charmander 2".
   - Combo the ramp shots to increase the combo multiplier.
   - Complete 6 ramp shots to light the Pokédex captive ball to complete the mode.
 
==TWEAKS==
 - Story Mode Progression
   - Play "Bulbasaur 1", "Squirtle 1", "Charizard 1", and "Pikachu vs. Raichu"
     to qualify one of the Story mini-wizard modes ("Pikachu vs. Lucario" or
    "Pikachu vs. Charizard") to start at the Pikachu ramp. 
     Shoot the Pikachu ramp to select and start either mini-wizard mode.
   - Play "Bulbasaur 2", "Squirtle 2", "Charizard 2", and "Pikachu vs. Mimikyu"
     to qualify the other story mini-wizard mode ("Pikachu vs. Lucario" or
    "Pikachu vs. Charizard") to start at the Pikachu ramp.

==SYSTEM 4.36==
 - Updated to nodeboard firmware/protocol v1.37.0
 - Various behind the scenes improvements for correctness and performance.

V.85 - 8/7/2026
=======================

==NEW==
 - Pokémon Arena
   - Complete the DISCOVER, CATCH, TRAIN, and BATTLE goals in all 4 biomes to qualify
     the "Pokémon Arena" mini-wizard mode to start at the Town scoop.
   - Pokémon Arena will be a Rival Battle with a handful of twists that are based on
     the rival Pokémon that is active. The rival Pokémon are battled in this order:
      * Ursaring	    
        - Trainer cannot switch Pokémon by hitting the Town scoop/target.
        - Each attack by Ursaring triggers a random switch of the Trainer's active Pokémon.
      * Sandslash	
        - Sandslash's Poison attack causes damage over time until the Trainer's Pokémon 
          faints, is switched, or healed.	
      * Talonflame
        - When Talonflame is in a flying state, the Trainer's attacks are disabled.
        - After Talonflame attacks, there is a brief period the Trainer Pokémon can attack.
      * Gengar - lights out
        - All gameplay lights are suppressed.
      * Metagross
        - Flippers are switched. Healing is disabled.	
      * Salamence
        - Salamence attacks strong and often.
        - Major shots still prevent attacks.
 - Pikachu vs. Lucario
   - Play "Bulbasaur 1", "Squirtle 1", "Charizard 1", and "Pikachu vs. Raichu"
     to qualify the "Pikachu vs. Lucario" and "Pikachu vs. Charizard" mini-wizard modes
     to start at the Pikachu ramp. Shoot the Pikachu ramp to select and start either 
     mini-wizard mode.
   - "Pikachu vs. Lucario" has 2 phases:
      * Build Phase 
        The Trainer can either increase jackpot value with YELLOW build shots or 
        lock a ball at the BLUE right ramp.  Once the Trainer locks enough balls or
        drains the single active ball, the multiball phase starts based on the number
        of locks during the build phase, with a jackpot based on the build shots 
        of the build phase.
      * Multiball Phase
        During the multiball phase, two random shots will be lit BLUE and when hit will
        randomly light somewhere else. Once enough shots are hit, the Trainer can lock
        a ball in the Pikachu ramp, and then score a super jackpot at the Poké Ball. 

==SYSTEM 4.33==
 - Fix an issue with the expression topper accessory lights on Spike3
 - Addressed a potential issue involving custom pricing with factional credits present at power-up
 - Updated to nodeboard firmware/protocol v1.35.0
 - Spike 3 netbridge 0.98.5
 - Various behind the scenes improvements for correctness and performance.

V.84 - 7/1/2026
=======================

==NEW==
 - Added Mode High Score Champions:
   - Team Rocket Multiball 2
   - Pickachu Hurry-Up
   - Squirtle Prize Pool
   - Charmander Super Spinner
   - Bulbasaur Loops

==TWEAKED==
 - Pokédex End-of-Ball animation shows count of Pokémon caught this ball.

==SYSTEM 4.28==
 - Various behind the scenes improvements for correctness and performance.

V.83 - 6/18/2026
=======================

==NEW==

 - Travel
    - Complete DISCOVER, CATCH, TRAIN, and BATTLE in the current biome
      to light TRAVEL at the Town Scoop.
    - When TRAVEL is lit, shoot the Town Scoop to choose which biome to explore next.

 - Added more Pokémon

 - Team Features
   - Complete the T-E-A-M bottom lanes to start a Team Feature. 
     Complete the Team Feature to boost the team member shot for the rest of the ball
     (shot score boosted, +1 Poké Ball per shot).
     - Pikachu Hurry-Up
       - Shoot right ramp to hold the ball.
       - While the ball is held, rapidly mash the action button to collect 
         the Pikachu Hurry-Up Award.
       - Complete the Pikachu Hurry-Up to boost the right ramp for the rest of the ball.
     - Squirtle Prize Pool
       - Shoot the left ramp to collect the Squirtle Prize Pool award.
       - Complete Squirtle Prize Pool to boost left ramp for the rest of the ball.
     - Charmander Super Spinner
       - Shoot the spinner to collect Charmander Super Spinner awards.
       - Complete Charmander Super Spinner to boost right orbit for the rest of the ball.
     - Bulbasaur Loops
       - Shoot the Bulbasaur loop to collect big points.
       - Complete Bulbasaur Loops to boost left orbit for the rest of the ball.

  - Team Rocket Multiball 2
    - After starting and playing Team Rocket Multiball 1, advance and start 
      Team Rocket Multiball 2 by completing the B-A-T-T-L-E targets and 
      battling the Team Rocket Balloon.

  - Magikarp Multiball (Topper Mode)
    - Collect the M-A-G-I-K-A-R-P letters on the topper by catching Pokémon. 
      The M-A-G-I-K-A-R-P letters carry over from player to player and game to game.
    - Collect all 8 letters to start Magikarp Multiball.

==TWEAKED==
 - Added more Meowth and Giovanni speech to Team Rocket rules and multiballs
 - Improved end-of-ball Pokédex user interface

==FIXED==
- Pikachu Vs Charizard - fixed a bug where all playfield lights were turned off and stayed off after making the final shot

==SYSTEM 4.27==
 - Nodeboard firmware/protocol v1.33.0
 - Added support for ToPS tournament in the Game Play Menu
 - Utilities Save/Load Menus now support local save slots for saving/restoring.
     If no USB drive is present, pressing ENTER will save to or load from the internal SD card.
     5 unique save slots are available.
 - Various behind the scenes improvements for correctness and performance.
 
V.82 - 5/6/2026
=======================

==NEW==
-Added Pokédex Assist
  -Hitting the Pokédex enough times will qualify Pokédex Assists
    -The strength of the hit will determine how much progress is earned
    -Progress is still available but lessened during multiballs
  -During Catch and Battle, the action button will flash red when available
    -During Catch, you can spot hurry-up shots except the final Catch shot
    -During Battle, you can Attack, but you cannot collect a Victory Bonus
  -A counter in the top right displays the stored number of Pokédex Assists
  -You can store up to 3 Pokédex Assists

-Added more Pokémon
-Added a ball save when a Pokémon is scanned (adjustable)
-Added game mode selection and adjustments
-Target game time added to service menu
-Lit outlane ball save now changes on flipper press (adjustable to slingshot)
-Added light effect for tilt warnings
-Competition install now effects various game features

==TWEAKED==
-Pikachu vs. Charizard
  -Scoring for each phase is now based on respective Story Mode scoring
  -Only two shots per phase are required to light captive ball to advance
    -Additional shots increase captive ball value
  -Final hurry up is based on collected jackpot values
  -Enhanced light shows and choreography

-Battles
  -Faint Jackpot removed from end of Battle sequence
  -Victory Bonus added
    -Collect a Victory Bonus at the Poké Ball after winning a Battle
    -Victory Bonus is based on performance during the Battle
  -Arena Bonus added
    -Arena Attack values partially add to the Arena Bonus
    -Shoot the center lane to collect and reset the Arena Bonus value
  -Healing added
    -Complete the Training bank once per appearance to heal your Pokémon
    -When your Pokémon faints or switches, Healing is re-enabled
  -Right flipper now cycles Pokémon for switching at the Town scoop
    -To qualifying switching, score 3 Attacks

-Discovery
  -Reduce default threshold for discovering a Pokémon
  -Increase progress for entering the pop bumper area

-Completing Training bank always adds 20 seconds during timed Story Modes
  -Story Mode timer will never exceed 60 seconds
-Decreased Pikachu vs. Raichu scoring
-Increased Team Rocket Multiball scoring
-Adjusted Squirtle 1 scoring to have higher ceiling
-Adjusted Charmander 1 to put more emphasis on spinner scoring
-Adjusted light effects for various playfield features
-Added more variety to attract light show
-Increased size of HSTD text

==FIXED==
-Improved top gate logic to avoid staying up unnecessarily long
-Increased pop bumper default firing time to address stuck ball issues
-Improved reliability of some devices
-Improved reliability of some display scenes
-Improved skill shot and valid playfield logic
-UI elements should now reset appropriately on mode start/end
-Charmander 1 spinner multiplier can't be modified during a spinner rip
-Ensure Battle animations are cleared before new Battles begin
-No longer offer Advance Discovery as a mystery award if Battle is lit
-Fixed a logic bug to play some previously suppressed Battle callouts
-Corrected Poké Ball servo device location on Premium/LE

==SYSTEM 4.24==
-Added "Test Menu Settings" to the "Machine Settings" category in the Graphical Service Menu.
 Allows customization of test screen colors, lamp test RGB behavior, and the starting menu selection.
-Updated to nodeboard firmware/protocol v1.33.0
-Various behind the scenes improvements for correctness and performance.


V.81 - 3/9/2026
=======================

- Initial release.

fields.software_name: Andrew Wilkening, Josh Henderson, Mitch Deason, Tanio Klyce
fields.machine_toys:
Pokémon-catching and collection system spanning four distinct habitats.
Persistent Pokémon collection through Stern Insider Connected, allowing players to retain captured Pokémon across compatible machines.
Four primary playable Pokémon: Pikachu, Bulbasaur, Squirtle, and Charmander, each with individual story modes and training mechanics.
Pokémon Rival Battles featuring different opponents, attack behaviors, and strategic character selection.
Interactive Team Rocket Meowth Balloon mechanism that descends into the battle arena during gameplay.
Pokédex captive-ball mechanism used to scan Pokémon and earn gameplay assists.
Poké Ball assembly used during Pokémon-catching sequences, with an animated ball-lock mechanism on Premium and Limited Edition models.
Animatronic Pikachu with synchronized movement and custom voice recordings on Premium and Limited Edition models.
Squirtle Whirlpool bowl mechanism on Premium and Limited Edition models.
Psyduck Sneak-In scoop on Premium and Limited Edition models, replaced by a stationary target on the Pro.
Interactive battle arena electromagnet on Premium and Limited Edition models.
Multiple Team Rocket and character-specific multiball modes.
Shot multipliers, Pokémon training, timed story modes, and progressive mini-wizard modes.
Footage from the original Pokémon animated television series.
Custom recorded speech for Pikachu and Team Rocket leader Giovanni.
Original Pokémon animated-series theme song.
Stern SPIKE 3 electronics platform.
Optional interactive Magikarp topper featuring an exclusive multiball mode.
Limited Edition production of 750 numbered machines, featuring upgraded cabinet lighting, mirrored backglass, enhanced audio, anti-reflection playfield glass, and factory-installed shaker motor.
fields.machine_comments:
Pokémon was Stern Pinball's first original cornerstone title of 2026, released during the Pokémon franchise's 30th anniversary year.
Pokémon was originally introduced in Japan in February 1996 with the release of Pokémon Red and Green for the Nintendo Game Boy.
The game was co-designed by George Gomez and Jack Danger, bringing together two Stern designers with notably different backgrounds and approaches to pinball design.
Unlike most modern Stern titles, the cabinet, backbox, translite, and playfield artwork were created primarily by The Pokémon Company International's internal art team rather than Stern's usual commissioned pinball artists.
The game draws heavily from the original Pokémon animated series rather than focusing exclusively on the franchise's video games or trading card game.
Stern incorporated footage from the original animated television series, along with the original Pokémon theme song and custom character recordings.
Pokémon marked Nintendo's return to licensed, commercially manufactured physical pinball machines after more than three decades.
Pokémon was announced on February 12, 2026, with the public reveal and commercial launch taking place during the franchise's anniversary year.
The game's launch was reportedly delayed by the extensive artwork and content approval process required by The Pokémon Company International.
Stern's design team confirmed that the 2026 release was intended to serve as the franchise's 30th anniversary pinball title, rather than being followed by a separately themed anniversary edition.
The game's persistent Pokémon collection was designed around Stern Insider Connected, allowing captured Pokémon to remain associated with a player's account between games and locations.
The Premium and Limited Edition models share the same primary playfield mechanisms, while the Limited Edition adds upgraded cabinet presentation, lighting, audio, and collector-oriented features.
The Limited Edition was restricted to 750 individually numbered machines worldwide.
The official Magikarp topper was released with its own exclusive multiball mode, making it a gameplay-expanding accessory rather than a purely decorative topper.
The Magikarp topper's letter-collection feature allows progress toward its exclusive multiball to persist between games and players.

fields.machine_videomode: he game's LCD display features animated Pokémon battles, Pokémon-catching sequences, original television-series footage, and other interactive presentations that accompany physical pinball gameplay. These sequences are integrated into the game's rules and do not constitute a separate video mode controlled independently of the pinball.

Update instructions - Games connected to Stern Insider Connected:
1 - Open the coin door and press the black/enter button to enter Test Mode.
2 - Using the 4 buttons on the coin door, navigate to the Stern Insider Connected Setup menu.
3 - Using the 4 buttons on the coin door, navigate down to the Software Update menu.
4 - If a software update is available, this page will give you the option to
    download and install it manually.  From this menu you can also select to install these
    updates automatically.

Update instructions - All Games:
1 - Download the zip file
2 - Unzip the file, this will create a folder that contains SPK file(s).
3 - Open the folder, copy the file(s) to the root level of a FAT32 formatted
    USB stick.  (Do not copy the folder.)
4 - Power game off
5 - Insert USB stick
6 - Turn on game
7 - After game boots up it will give the option for software update
8 - Volume buttons change options for full or quick update. Enter selects the
    option and starts the update.
9 - Once update is completed game will prompt user to power game off and
    remove USB stick.

fields.machine_comments:
Stern's second Transformers pinball machine, following the 2011 game based on the live-action film franchise.
Based primarily on the original Generation 1 Transformers animated series, which debuted in 1984.
Released during the 40th anniversary year of The Transformers: The Movie (1986).
Features custom voice recordings by Peter Cullen as Optimus Prime and Frank Welker as Megatron and Soundwave.
Includes "The Touch" by Stan Bush, originally featured in the 1986 animated film.
Features original music from Knights of Unicron.
The game introduced the Cyber Coin system, allowing Insider Connected players to earn virtual currency and unlock special challenge modes.
Features Stern's first simultaneous head-to-head, split-flipper competitive challenge mode, Optimus vs. Megatron.
The Limited Edition was restricted to 750 units worldwide.
LE machines feature a designer-autographed bottom arch and signed Certificate of Authenticity.
The game was designed by Elliot Eismin, with software by Elizabeth Gieske and Mike Kyzivat.
Game software version 0.89 introduced the topper-exclusive Ghost in the Machine challenge mode.
Game software version 0.92 introduced Prime Training.
Game software version 0.94 introduced Optimus vs. Megatron split-flipper competition.

fields.machine_videomode: No traditional video mode has been confirmed. The game includes several standalone challenge modes accessed through the game's menu, including Prime Training, The Movie: The Mode, Optimus vs. Megatron, and the topper-exclusive Ghost in the Machine. These feature interactive playfield gameplay rather than traditional display-only video games.

    updates automatically.

Update instructions - All Games:
1 - Download the zip file
2 - Unzip the file, this will create a folder that contains SPK file(s).
3 - Open the folder, copy the file(s) to the root level of a FAT32 formatted
    USB stick.  (Do not copy the folder.)
4 - Power game off
5 - Insert USB stick
6 - Turn on game
7 - After game boots up it will give the option for software update

Version 0.94.0 - Sep 30, 2026 - Optimus vs Megatron aka The Split Flipper Mode 
-----------------------------
==New==
  -OPTIMUS VS MEGATRON
    -Added this new stand-alone challenge mode, specifically designed for 2-Player (via split-flipper).
    -How split-flipper works:
      -Player 1 operates the left flipper. Player 2 operates the right flipper.
      -Both players play at the same time.
    -How the mode works:      
      -Player 1 plays as Optimus Prime. Player 2 as Megatron.
      -Each player has their own health bar.      
      -Player 1 aims for RED shots to hit their opponent, while Player 2 aims for PURPLE.      
      -Once a player's health reaches 0 (or the timer runs out), the round is over. 
      -Winner is decided by best of 3 timed rounds.   
      -Round 2 introduces a new rule, TEAM-ATTACK:
        -Shoot targets to light the action button. 
          -RED targets light button RED. PURPLE targets light button PURPLE.
        -Rapidly hit the action button to build TEAM-ATTACK meter.
          -Action button will unlight after 2 seconds.
        -Team-Attacks automatically inflict damage once meter reaches 100%.              
      -Round 3 is a combination of the previous two rounds.
      -Each round adds another ball in play (eg. Round 1 is single ball. Round 3 is 3-ball).

    -Challenge modes are only accessible from the gameplay menu.
      -hit the yellow action button and navigate with the flippers to access.

==TWEAKS==
  -Prime Training
    -Flipper Skills: if the action button hasn't been used, a callout prompts the player after 10 seconds.
    -Flipper Skills: if the player still isn't using the action button, the demo advances on their behalf every 15 seconds.    
  -Center orbit is no longer ignored right after a plunge (tightened the timer).    
  -Show associated award video after the space bridge sequence runs (not before).
  -Added various sfx and text based improvements.

==BUGS==
  -Fixed a rare crash bug on the mystery award.
  -Fixed the wrong tech spec background video playing in rare cases.
  -Allow Dinobot Multiball background to play during Prime Training.

==OPTIMUS VS MEGATRON CONTINUED==
  -Rubberbanding mechanics:
    -More shots appear for the losing player (at varying health thresholds).
    -Draining will slightly hurt the player in the lead during Round 1 and 2.
  -Once a shot is collected, it temporarily unlights.
  -Shooting the Grimlock ramp will automatically hold up the upper-right flipper.
    -This allows the ball to feed down to the left flipper.
  -Flipping the left flipper will always automatically lower the upper-right flipper.   
  -Shooting a lit target while the action button is lit for the opposing side will unlight the action button.
  -The game does not register which player hit which shot (you can hit yourself).   
  -The location selection does not affect the mode. It is purely aesthetic.   
  -All values (damage per round, team-up inc, timers, etc.) can be changed through the adjustments submenu.

==SYSTEM 4.37==
  -Various behind the scenes improvements for correctness and performance.

Custom sculpted Optimus Prime bash toy with voice recordings by Peter Cullen.
Soundwave cassette-tape ball lock and ball-ejection mechanism.
Animatronic Megatron with articulated, rotating pinball-firing fusion cannon (Premium/LE).
Static Megatron robot toy (Pro).
Three-bank drop targets protecting Megatron.
Optimus Prime V.U.K. feeds Soundwave for ball locks and Transformers Multiball.
Energon optical spinner awards Energon Cubes used to enhance missions.
Sculpted Grimlock Dinobot toy and associated ramp.
Left Grimlock crossover shot feeding the upper-right flipper.
Three flippers, including an upper-right flipper.
Two slingshots.
Physical Add-a-Ball ball-lock post.
Five story-driven missions inspired by the original Transformers animated series.
Collectible Transformers Tech Spec cards.
Dinobot, Combiner, and Transformers-themed multiball modes.
Original Transformers animated television footage and character dialogue.
Cyber Coin virtual currency system through Stern Insider Connected.
Prime Training practice and skill-development challenge mode.
Optimus vs. Megatron two-player split-flipper challenge mode.
The Movie: The Mode, featuring music from the 1986 animated film.
18.5-inch full-HD LCD display.
Stern Insider Connected integration.
Full-color mirrored backglass, Expression Lighting, shaker motor, and upgraded speaker system (LE).
Limited Edition production of 750 individually numbered machines.
fields.machine_comments:
Stern's second Transformers pinball machine, following the 2011 game based on the live-action film franchise.
Based primarily on the original Generation 1 Transformers animated series, which debuted in 1984.
Released during the 40th anniversary year of The Transformers: The Movie (1986).
Features custom voice recordings by Peter Cullen as Optimus Prime and Frank Welker as Megatron and Soundwave.
Includes "The Touch" by Stan Bush, originally featured in the 1986 animated film.
Features original music from Knights of Unicron.
The game introduced the Cyber Coin system, allowing Insider Connected players to earn virtual currency and unlock special challenge modes.
Features Stern's first simultaneous head-to-head, split-flipper competitive challenge mode, Optimus vs. Megatron.
The Limited Edition was restricted to 750 units worldwide.
LE machines feature a designer-autographed bottom arch and signed Certificate of Authenticity.
The game was designed by Elliot Eismin, with software by Elizabeth Gieske and Mike Kyzivat.
Game software version 0.89 introduced the topper-exclusive Ghost in the Machine challenge mode.
Game software version 0.92 introduced Prime Training.
Game software version 0.94 introduced Optimus vs. Megatron split-flipper competition.
fields.machine_ornament: An officially licensed Optimus Prime topper was released by Stern in July 2026. The topper features a mechanically animated Optimus Prime bust with illuminated eyes and body details, synchronized with voice recordings by Peter Cullen. It also unlocks the
fields.machine_videomode: No traditional video mode has been confirmed. The game includes several standalone challenge modes accessed through the game's menu, including Prime Training, The Movie: The Mode, Optimus vs. Megatron, and the topper-exclusive Ghost in the Machine. These feature interactive playfield gameplay rather than traditional display-only video games.

fields.machine_toys:
Heart & Dagger Magnetic Ball Catch: Large sculpted Heart & Dagger mechanism featuring a magnetic ball grab, three vertical positions, and a mechanical release that directs the ball onto different ramps and wireforms.
Shot Through the Heart: Interactive center shot incorporating the Heart & Dagger mechanism and three-level diverter, allowing balls to travel along different paths depending on the mechanism's position.
Steel Horse Three-Ball Lock: Hidden magnet along the back orbit diverts balls into a vertical upkicker feeding a physical three-ball lock.
Backstage Access: Multifunctional playfield area featuring three standup targets, a spinner, hidden scoop, exit ramp, magnetic ball catch, and a second physical three-ball lock.
Crowd Amp-Up Loop: Unique 360-degree loop-the-loop captive ball mechanism featuring an integrated spinner activated by striking the captive ball.
Crowd Surf Jump Ramp: Left outlane recovery mechanism featuring a miniature flipper that launches balls up a metal jump ramp and back into play.
Sound Board Apron: Interactive concert soundboard featuring an illuminated cassette deck, VU meter, switch, and motorized fader sliders that physically move during gameplay.
Lightning Flippers: Two shortened 2-7/8-inch main flippers designed to create faster gameplay and more demanding ball control than conventional three-inch flippers.
Four-Flipper Layout: Two main Lightning Flippers and two additional miniature flippers provide access to upper playfield shots and the Crowd Surf mechanism.
Physical Ball Locks: Two separate three-ball locking mechanisms integrated into the Steel Horse and Backstage Access assemblies.
Three Magnetic Gameplay Locations: Independent magnetic ball-control systems incorporated into the Heart & Dagger mechanism, Steel Horse orbit, and Backstage area.
Concert Stage Lighting: Custom metal trusses with three functional spotlights and an illuminated Bon Jovi stage sign featuring RGBW backlighting.
Horizon Atmospheric Lighting: Integrated RGBW inner-cabinet lighting system that synchronizes with music, modes, and concert effects.
Jon Bon Jovi Guitar Sculpture: Detailed representation of Jon Bon Jovi's iconic New Jersey guitar positioned above the captive ball mechanism.
Seventeen Licensed Songs: Full-length recordings spanning Bon Jovi's career, accompanied by music videos, live concert footage, and custom lighting sequences.
Setlist Building: Song-selection and progression system allowing players to build a concert setlist while completing music-themed gameplay objectives.
Premium Audio System: Custom audio package featuring stereo speakers, an eight-inch cabinet subwoofer, and enhanced sound reproduction for music and concert footage.
Standard Premium Equipment: Factory-installed shaker motor, anti-reflective Infinity Glass, inner cabinet art blades, EverGloss cabinet decals, and RGBW playfield illumination.
fields.machine_comments:
Bon Jovi was officially announced on July 28, 2026, as Barrels of Fun's fourth commercial pinball release, following Labyrinth, Dune, and Winchester Mystery House.
The game is Barrels of Fun's first music-themed pinball machine.
Production is limited to 700 machines worldwide. Barrels of Fun confirmed the 700-unit limit again following the 2026 Chicago Pinball Expo.
The game was designed by David Van Es, who previously designed Jim Henson's Labyrinth and Dune for Barrels of Fun.
Artwork was created by Canadian artist Jonathan Bergeron, professionally known as Johnny Crap, whose illustration work frequently incorporates rock music, horror, and pop culture.
The game's 17-song soundtrack spans more than four decades of Bon Jovi's career, from Runaway (1984) through Legendary (2024).
The game includes both Livin' on a Prayer and You Give Love a Bad Name, two of the band's signature songs from the 1986 album Slippery When Wet.
The Heart & Dagger mechanism is inspired by the band's iconic heart-and-dagger logo, which appeared prominently on the cover of the 1988 album New Jersey.
The Steel Horse mechanism references the lyrics of Wanted Dead or Alive, one of Bon Jovi's signature songs.
The game features a working miniature soundboard built into the apron, with motorized audio faders that physically move during gameplay.
The Crowd Amp-Up mechanism combines a captive ball, a complete 360-degree loop, and an internal spinner, an unusual combination of mechanical features.
The Crowd Surf mechanism uses a miniature flipper in the left outlane to launch balls up a jump ramp and return them to the playfield.
The two primary flippers are Lightning Flippers, measuring approximately 2-7/8 inches instead of the conventional 3 inches. Their shorter length increases the difficulty of ball saves and controlled shots.
Unlike many modern licensed music machines, Bon Jovi was offered in a single fully equipped model rather than separate Pro, Premium, and Limited Edition versions.
The game includes a factory-installed shaker motor, anti-reflective playfield glass, inner cabinet artwork, upgraded audio system, and concert lighting as standard equipment.
The original manufacturer's suggested retail price was $12,000, with a $2,000 deposit required to reserve a machine.
Bon Jovi made a prominent appearance at the 2026 Chicago Pinball Expo, where Barrels of Fun reported strong player interest and limited remaining distributor inventory.
fields.machine_ornament: No official factory topper or additional backbox ornament has been announced for Bon Jovi. The backbox features custom artwork, a 15.6-inch HD LCD display, illuminated stereo speakers, and laser-cut Heart & Dagger speaker grilles. RGBW lighting provi
fields.machine_videomode: No standalone video mode has been documented for Bon Jovi. The game's 15.6-inch LCD display presents licensed music videos, live concert footage, song-selection menus, animated sequences, scoring information, and mode-specific graphics. Visual effects are synchronized with gameplay, stage lighting, and the game's 17-song soundtrack. Song-based objectives are completed through physical playfield shots rather than separate video-only challenges.

fields.machine_toys:
- RPG-inspired pinball gameplay featuring character classes, experience points, leveling, equipment, inventory, and branching storylines.
- Stern PinSave system, allowing players to save character progression, inventory, and campaign progress through Insider Connected and resume on other connected machines.
- Four initial playable character classes: Paladin, Wizard, Cleric, and Rogue, with Ranger, Barbarian, and Bard unlockable through campaign progression.
- Campaign featuring 10 locations across Faerûn, more than 45 different monsters, 21 story modes, multiple wizard modes, and three possible endings.
- Rath the Relentless, a sculpted red dragon featuring illuminated eyes and hit detection. Premium and Limited Edition models include multi-axis movement and the ability to launch pinballs from the dragon's mouth.
- Player-controlled metal shield that rises between the flippers to defend against attacks and assist with gameplay.
- Electromagnet-powered Gelatinous Cube mechanism that captures and holds the pinball.
- Dungeon Crawl mode featuring procedurally generated five-level dungeons, treasure, monsters, and traps. Premium and Limited Edition models feature a mechanically rising dungeon entrance.
- Three-flipper playfield featuring multiple ramps, loops, diverters, hidden passages, and interactive mechanisms.
- Critical Hit captive-ball target used during battles and other gameplay features.
- Fizmo's Store, allowing players to purchase equipment and items to improve their characters.
- Tiny's Tavern, featuring a spinner-controlled dice game of chance.
- Hidden Temple shot behind the upper flipper that activates double scoring.
- Mountain Passage up/down ramp and an elevated Bridge ramp connecting sections of the playfield.
- Multiple multiball modes, including Dragon Multiball and Gelatinous Cube Multiball.
- Cooperative gameplay allowing multiple players to share campaign progression during a game.
- Tournament mode that disables saved campaign progression and standardizes random gameplay elements.
- Weekly variations in dungeon layouts, character statistics, treasure contents, and shop inventories.
- More than 100 collectible trinkets providing gameplay enhancements and special abilities.
- Original hand-drawn artwork by Vincent Proce, display animations by Paul Chamnankit, and an orchestral soundtrack composed by Cris Velasco.
- Voice performances by Michael Dorn, Kevin Smith, Luke Gygax, Matthew Mercer, Laura Bailey, Marisha Ray, Gerard Way, Brendon Small, and others.
- Optional interactive Treasure Chest topper featuring an animated Mimic, exclusive Mimic Mania mode, and additional playable character.
fields.machine_comments:
- Dungeons & Dragons: The Tyrant's Eye was officially announced on January 3, 2025, as part of the 50th anniversary celebration of the Dungeons & Dragons tabletop role-playing game, originally published in 1974.
- The game was designed by Brian Eddy, whose previous pinball designs include Medieval Madness (1997), Attack from Mars (1995), Stranger Things (2019), and Venom (2023).
- The game was developed in collaboration with Hasbro and Wizards of the Coast, the companies responsible for the Dungeons & Dragons franchise.
- The Limited Edition production quantity of 740 machines was chosen as a tribute to 1974, the year Dungeons & Dragons was originally published.
- The game's setting is the Forgotten Realms, a fantasy campaign world created by Ed Greenwood and first published by TSR in 1987.
- The primary antagonist, Tiamat, is a five-headed dragon goddess who has appeared throughout the history of Dungeons & Dragons.
- The game incorporates traditional Dungeons & Dragons role-playing elements, including character classes, experience points, dice rolls, ability statistics, armor class, equipment, and branching campaign decisions.
- Stern introduced its PinSave system with Dungeons & Dragons, allowing players to save character levels, equipment, and campaign progress through Insider Connected and continue their adventure on other connected machines.
- The game's campaign features three different endings, each unlocking an additional playable character class.
- Procedurally generated Dungeon Crawl layouts change weekly, along with character statistics, equipment locations, treasure chest contents, and shop inventories.
- Michael Dorn, best known for portraying Worf in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, provides the voice of Rath the Relentless.
- The voice cast includes performers associated with Critical Role, including Matthew Mercer, Laura Bailey, and Marisha Ray.
- Luke Gygax, son of Dungeons & Dragons co-creator Gary Gygax, contributed voice work to the game.
- Gerard Way, lead vocalist of My Chemical Romance and creator of The Umbrella Academy, is among the game's voice performers.
- Original music was composed by Cris Velasco, whose work includes music for God of War, Mass Effect, and other video games.
- The Limited Edition includes exclusive cabinet artwork, a mirrored backglass, Dragon Red powder-coated armor, upgraded audio, and a numbered identification plaque.
- Stern released an interactive Treasure Chest topper featuring a transforming Mimic mechanism, an exclusive Mimic Mania mode, and an additional playable Fighter character voiced by Brendon Small.
- The game features a three-flipper layout, with the upper flipper used to access elevated ramps, loops, and hidden playfield shots.
fields.machine_ornament: Stern released an officially licensed Treasure Chest topper for Dungeons & Dragons: The Tyrant's Eye, compatible with Pro, Premium, and Limited Edition models. The topper features a motorized treasure chest that opens to reveal either glittering trea
fields.machine_videomode: Dungeons & Dragons: The Tyrant's Eye features Dungeon Crawl, a hybrid video and physical playfield mode. Players navigate procedurally generated, five-level dungeons displayed on the LCD, choosing paths to discover treasure, battle monsters, and avoid traps. Dungeon layouts and rewards change weekly, encouraging exploration and repeated play. The mode incorporates physical pinball shots and, on Premium and Limited Edition models, a mechanically rising dungeon entrance that captures the ball. The game also features animated character battles, dice rolls, story sequences, and campaign decisions displayed on the LCD.

** NOTE - HOW TO RESET ONE CHARACTER **
This will reset only ONE of your characters.

To access the GAME PLAY MENU and RESET ONE CHARACTER:
 - 1 - While the game is connected and between games
 - 2 - Hit the Action Button to enter the GAME PLAY MENU.
 - 3 - Press the left flipper until you arrive at RESET ONE CHARACTER.
 - 4 - Select it with the ACTION BUTTON.
 - 5 - Scan your QR code and the game will load all your saved characters.
 - 6 - Use the flipper buttons to select the character you want to
       reset and hit the ACTION BUTTON.
 - 7 - The game will ask you if you are sure. If you are not sure
       you can hit any flipper to back out.


** NOTE - HOW TO DELETE A TRINKET **
To access the GAME PLAY MENU and Delete a TRINKET:
 - 1 - While the game is connected and between games
 - 2 - Hit the Action Button to enter the GAME PLAY MENU.
 - 3 - Press the left flipper until you arrive at DELETE TRINKET.
 - 4 - Select it with the ACTION BUTTON.
 - 5 - Scan your QR code to enter a prompt.
 - 6 - Use flippers to change which Trinket you would like to delete.
 - 7 - Hit the Action Button to select it and the game will ask you if you are
       sure. If you are not sure you can hit any flipper to back out.
 - 8 - If you change your mind about deleting a Trinket you can hold a flipper
       button in to speed up the timer and end the prompt.


** NOTE - HOW TO SEE THE CUTSCENE GALLERY **
To access the GAME PLAY MENU and Get to the Cut scene Gallery:
 - 1 - While between games.
 - 2 - Hit the Action Button to enter the GAME PLAY MENU.
 - 3 - Press the left flipper until you arrive at CUTSCENE GALLERY.
 - 4 - Select it with the ACTION BUTTON.
 - 5 - Use the flipper buttons to navigate to the cut scene you want to view.
 - 6 - Hit the Action button to start the cut scene
 - 7 - Hold both flipper buttons to end the mode.


** NOTE - HOW TO USE THE DJ MIXER   **
To access the GAME PLAY MENU for DJ MIXER:
 - 1 - On a non-location game and between games.
 - 2 - Hit the Action Button to enter the GAME PLAY MENU.

***  NEW  ***
    - Changed how Dragon Multiball works:
        - Levels are now a form of campaign progression and the max level is
          increased to 10. The first time you face the Dragon with a character,
          he will be at level 1. Each time you beat a dragon the level will go 
          up to a maximum of 10 levels.

        - Levels increase on successfully defeating the dragon, and resets to 1 
          on campaign completion.
          - Each Character has their own Dragon Multiball level. It only rises
            when that character beats it.

        - As you progress through the levels a few things change:
            - You need additional hits to the Dragon to win. One additional hit
              at level 2, climbing to 16 additional hits at level 10.
            - The Dragon needs less drains to win. At levels 7 and 8 he needs
              one less drain, and levels 9 and 10 he needs 2 less.
            - (PREM/LE) Starting with Level 3 The Dragon will pool the balls
              within it and spitting them out in groups of 3. This means there
              will be time with less balls on the playfield from time to time.

        - As you increase the level the Super Jackpot becomes more important:
            - The Jackpot shots needed to light Super Jackpot DECREASE as you
              gain levels. Starting at 5-shots for level one down to 2-shots by
              levels 9 and 10.
            - The Base Value of the Super Jackpot increases with each level. It
              starts at 3 Million and climbs to 8 Million at level ten.
            - Collecting a Super Jackpot will also count as hitting the dragon.
              You will earn one hit from Super Jackpots at level 1. Climbing to
              6 hits on the dragon for each Super Jackpot at level 8 and
              beyond.
            - (PREM/LE) Starting at 6th level the Dragon will block the Super
              Jackpot shot until you hit him.
            - Town Celebration Super Jackpot base value will also increase with
              each level.

        - Also:
            - Added speech to the starting Display.
            - Increased volume of the sound effect of hitting the dragon.
            - Super Jackpot has speech when lit.
            - Super Jackpot has all 3 arrows red instead of just the Super
              jackpot insert.
            - Super Jackpot grants a shield use when collected.
            - Starting display effect can now be blow off with flippers.
            - The left loop (RED CAVE) No longer has a regular jackpot. The
              right loop (SHORTCUT) has one instead.
            - Changed the choreography of when the balls kick out at start

    - Added 7 Achievements: 
     Dragonforged: Paladin	 - Defeat Level 10 in Dragon Multiball as a Paladin

    - Changed the main rules for lighting Dragon Multiball:
        - Hit 3-bank of targets to spell DRAGON. Complete DRAGON to light
          DRAGON MULTIBALL.
        - The first time the game may spot some letters for you if the
          difficulty adjustment is set to Medium or Easy. Also, there are
          Trinkets that will add spotted letters too.

          letter.

    - Added more monsters to Traveling:

          overworld traveling.

          When encountering a monster while traveling in the overworld there is
          a 33% chance each to encounter wolves, an Owlbear or Earth
          Elementals.

          If the player character is level 7 or higher Elemental Myrmidon
          replaces the normal Earth Elementals. Additionally, at level 7 or
          higher, Will-o-wisps will replace wolves half the time.

        - Added Driders, Giant Spiders, and Intellect Devourers to Underdark
          traveling.
    
          When encountering a monster in the Underdark, there is a 33% chance
          each to encounter a Roper, an Intellect Devourers or Giant Spiders.
           
          If the player character is level 7 or higher, Driders have a 50%
          chance to spawn instead of Giant Spiders.

***  NEW  ***
   - In the Battle of Gauntlgrym, if you choose to go after Balinor, your path

   - Added THE UNDERMOUNTAIN as the 3rd ending of the game.
     - You can come here from a choice you made in The Lich of Dragonspear
       Castle, or a choice you made in The Battle of Gauntlgrym.
     - This Wizard mode has 6 LEVELS!
           - First, after you descend down from the Yawning Portal, you need to
             find the correct door.
           - Next your path is interrupted by your 5 armed friends. 
           - Using their portal, you leave the dungeon and arrive in the town
             of Skullport where you are asked for a toll from some BugBears.
             If you have enough gold, you can pay them with the left loop shot.
             If you don't have enough gold or don't want to pay, you can fight
             them normally.
           - Now some Flaming Skulls stop your progress in town. After you deal
             with some of them a Mezzoloth shows up and tells you to follow
             him. Now you need to shoot white shots to disengage from the
             seemingly infinite Flaming Skulls.
           - Following the Mezzoloth to a warehouse might have been a mistake.
             They ambush you! After you kill them, searching the place recovers 
             your health potions and the way forward.
           - Finding a new exit that leads the lair of Xanathar. He is not
             happy that you have made it that far. Each of his eye stalks need
             to be defeated in order by hitting them normally or using a ranged
             weapon. Be careful because some of the attacks by the eye stalks
             have strange effects:
                    - Darkness to dim the battlefield
                    - Hurry Up opportunities
                    - Flipper Inverting Confusion
                    - Amazing amounts of damage to one target.
                    - Large Area of effect blast to damage the whole party
             Then, when you think you have killed Xanathar, Lasandra realizes
             it was not the real one! The real Xanathar shows up and you have
             to beat him one more time.
     - Each new level will start the ball saver for a few seconds.
     - When you are between levels and there are green shots lit you can
       shoot them to heal your party.
     - If you complete THE UNDERMOUNTAIN, you will unlock The Ranger as a
       character you can play.

   - Added Rhyme the Ranger as a playable character.
     - Rangers are good at using a ranged weapon.
       - They get two moving blue arrows when holding down the action button to
         aim at monsters. If either or both blue arrows line up with monster
         they will hit one or both.
       - If they have the Occulus Bow, the Ranger will have 3 blue arrows that
         move back and forth helping you aim.
     - Rangers feature Dexterity and Wisdom. Dexterity helps your armor class,
       making it harder to be hit. and Dexterity adds to your ranged weapon 
       Damage. Your wisdom adds time to all your timers.
     - You need to complete THE UNDERMOUNTAIN to unlock this character.

   - The Barbarian now does extra damage to all Fiends: Abashi and
     Yugoloths. He just doesn't like them.

   - Added lamp effects for
           - Dungeon Crawl Start and End
           - Unlocking a Character
           - Looting a Treasure Chest and finding a Magic Item

LE/PREMIUM V0.96 - SEPTEMBER 23, 2025
=====================================
***  NEW  ***
   - Added The Battle Of Gauntlgrym
       - Balinor and his Zhenterium are at the castle gates of the Dwarven King
         Raddok.
       - You need to complete White 3: ACQUIRE LIFEBLOOD ARMOR and Puprple 3: 
         SLAAD ASSASSINS to enable.
       - This wizard mode has 4 or 5 phases depending your choice.
           - First you have to kill Zhent Soldiers. Kill them fast. The longer
             you take the more powerful they get.
           - Next you will face Red Slaad. Each time they attack they will move
             and regenerate some of their health. So do not let them attack.
           - Next you face Hobgoblins. They fight in packs and are stronger if
             they are next to each other on the playfield.
           - Next you will have a choice:
               - Choose to stay and help Nighdaar and you will face Minotaurs.
               - Choose to help King Raddok and you will have to face two
                 Skeleton Minotaurs before facing Balinor himself.
               - A Skeleton will reconstitute when one it is killed if the 2nd
                 one is not killed first.
               - If Balinor has the Lifeblood Armor, You will have to destroy
                 that first. Then your attacks will do damage to him.
               - Every few seconds that Balinor is not attacked he will launch
                 a firebolt from his gauntlet.
       - When you are between phases and there are green shots lit you can
         shoot them to heal your party.

   - Added Rescue The King
       - Balinor has captured King Raddok. You must find a way into the castle
         and Rescue him.
       - You need to complete The Battle of Gauntlgrym to enable.
       - This is one of 3 endings of the game.
       - This wizard mode has 7 Levels!

fields.machine_toys:
- RPG-inspired pinball gameplay featuring character classes, experience points, leveling, equipment, inventory, and branching storylines.
- Stern PinSave system, allowing players to save character progression, inventory, and campaign progress through Insider Connected and resume on other connected machines.
- Four initial playable character classes: Paladin, Wizard, Cleric, and Rogue, with Ranger, Barbarian, and Bard unlockable through campaign progression.
- Campaign featuring 10 locations across Faerûn, more than 45 different monsters, 21 story modes, multiple wizard modes, and three possible endings.
- Rath the Relentless, a sculpted red dragon featuring illuminated eyes and hit detection. Premium and Limited Edition models include multi-axis movement and the ability to launch pinballs from the dragon's mouth.
- Player-controlled metal shield that rises between the flippers to defend against attacks and assist with gameplay.
- Electromagnet-powered Gelatinous Cube mechanism that captures and holds the pinball.
- Dungeon Crawl mode featuring procedurally generated five-level dungeons, treasure, monsters, and traps. Premium and Limited Edition models feature a mechanically rising dungeon entrance.
- Three-flipper playfield featuring multiple ramps, loops, diverters, hidden passages, and interactive mechanisms.
- Critical Hit captive-ball target used during battles and other gameplay features.
- Fizmo's Store, allowing players to purchase equipment and items to improve their characters.
- Tiny's Tavern, featuring a spinner-controlled dice game of chance.
- Hidden Temple shot behind the upper flipper that activates double scoring.
- Mountain Passage up/down ramp and an elevated Bridge ramp connecting sections of the playfield.
- Multiple multiball modes, including Dragon Multiball and Gelatinous Cube Multiball.
- Cooperative gameplay allowing multiple players to share campaign progression during a game.
- Tournament mode that disables saved campaign progression and standardizes random gameplay elements.
- Weekly variations in dungeon layouts, character statistics, treasure contents, and shop inventories.
- More than 100 collectible trinkets providing gameplay enhancements and special abilities.
- Original hand-drawn artwork by Vincent Proce, display animations by Paul Chamnankit, and an orchestral soundtrack composed by Cris Velasco.
- Voice performances by Michael Dorn, Kevin Smith, Luke Gygax, Matthew Mercer, Laura Bailey, Marisha Ray, Gerard Way, Brendon Small, and others.
- Optional interactive Treasure Chest topper featuring an animated Mimic, exclusive Mimic Mania mode, and additional playable character.
fields.machine_comments:
- Dungeons & Dragons: The Tyrant's Eye was officially announced on January 3, 2025, as part of the 50th anniversary celebration of the Dungeons & Dragons tabletop role-playing game, originally published in 1974.
- The game was designed by Brian Eddy, whose previous pinball designs include Medieval Madness (1997), Attack from Mars (1995), Stranger Things (2019), and Venom (2023).
- The game was developed in collaboration with Hasbro and Wizards of the Coast, the companies responsible for the Dungeons & Dragons franchise.
- The Limited Edition production quantity of 740 machines was chosen as a tribute to 1974, the year Dungeons & Dragons was originally published.
- The game's setting is the Forgotten Realms, a fantasy campaign world created by Ed Greenwood and first published by TSR in 1987.
- The primary antagonist, Tiamat, is a five-headed dragon goddess who has appeared throughout the history of Dungeons & Dragons.
- The game incorporates traditional Dungeons & Dragons role-playing elements, including character classes, experience points, dice rolls, ability statistics, armor class, equipment, and branching campaign decisions.
- Stern introduced its PinSave system with Dungeons & Dragons, allowing players to save character levels, equipment, and campaign progress through Insider Connected and continue their adventure on other connected machines.
- The game's campaign features three different endings, each unlocking an additional playable character class.
- Procedurally generated Dungeon Crawl layouts change weekly, along with character statistics, equipment locations, treasure chest contents, and shop inventories.
- Michael Dorn, best known for portraying Worf in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, provides the voice of Rath the Relentless.
- The voice cast includes performers associated with Critical Role, including Matthew Mercer, Laura Bailey, and Marisha Ray.
- Luke Gygax, son of Dungeons & Dragons co-creator Gary Gygax, contributed voice work to the game.
- Gerard Way, lead vocalist of My Chemical Romance and creator of The Umbrella Academy, is among the game's voice performers.
- Original music was composed by Cris Velasco, whose work includes music for God of War, Mass Effect, and other video games.
- The Limited Edition includes exclusive cabinet artwork, a mirrored backglass, Dragon Red powder-coated armor, upgraded audio, and a numbered identification plaque.
- Stern released an interactive Treasure Chest topper featuring a transforming Mimic mechanism, an exclusive Mimic Mania mode, and an additional playable Fighter character voiced by Brendon Small.
- The game features a three-flipper layout, with the upper flipper used to access elevated ramps, loops, and hidden playfield shots.

Players navigate procedurally generated, five-level dungeons displayed on the LCD, choosing paths to discover treasure, battle monsters, and avoid traps. Dungeon layouts and rewards change weekly, encouraging exploration and repeated play.         - Collecting a Treasure Chest on a machine with a topper awards 1

          not to a player.

          Tiny's Tavern shot. Starting the mode reveals it to be Mimic Mania.

          mode isn't lost easily.
        - The first stage is the Gold Treasure stage. 
                - Shooting the gold shots awards Gold, Points and builds the
                  Mimic Value. 
                - This stage ends with a timer.
        - The second stage is the Blue Advance stage. 
                - The player must lock both balls by shooting the blue shots. 
                - Locking the first ball starts a timer and lites additional
                  shots. 
                - The timer ending simply releases the locked ball. Both balls
                  must be locked at the same time to advance.
        - After locking both balls there is a random chance to what happens. 
                - There is a high chance to get a chest that awards points and
                  gold before returning to the Gold Treasure Stage. 
                - Otherwise, the chest is a mimic that starts the next stage.
                  The chance of a mimic grows with each Blue Advance Stage.
        - The final stage is the White Mimic stage. 
                - During this phase, there is a red shot on the left eject and 
                  white shots everywhere else. 
                - Shooting the white shots builds the Mimic Value at a higher  
                  rate than during the Gold Treasure stage.
                - Shooting the red shot ends the mode and awards the Mimic
                  Value with a multiplier value equal to the remaining party
                  members.
                - A timer counts down during this mode. When it ends, the Mimic
                  eats a party member which lowers the multiplier value.
                - If the mimic eats all 4 party members, the mode ends and the 
                  player loses out on the Mimic Value.

    - Changed how Dragon Multiball works:

              starts at 3 Million and climbs to 8 Million at level ten.

              6 hits on the dragon for each Super Jackpot at level 8 and
              beyond.

              Jackpot shot until you hit him.

fields.machine_toys:
- RPG-inspired pinball gameplay featuring character classes, experience points, leveling, equipment, inventory, and branching storylines.
- Stern PinSave system, allowing players to save character progression, inventory, and campaign progress through Insider Connected and resume on other connected machines.
- Four initial playable character classes: Paladin, Wizard, Cleric, and Rogue, with Ranger, Barbarian, and Bard unlockable through campaign progression.
- Campaign featuring 10 locations across Faerûn, more than 45 different monsters, 21 story modes, multiple wizard modes, and three possible endings.
- Rath the Relentless, a sculpted red dragon featuring illuminated eyes and hit detection. Premium and Limited Edition models include multi-axis movement and the ability to launch pinballs from the dragon's mouth.
- Player-controlled metal shield that rises between the flippers to defend against attacks and assist with gameplay.
- Electromagnet-powered Gelatinous Cube mechanism that captures and holds the pinball.
- Dungeon Crawl mode featuring procedurally generated five-level dungeons, treasure, monsters, and traps. Premium and Limited Edition models feature a mechanically rising dungeon entrance.
- Three-flipper playfield featuring multiple ramps, loops, diverters, hidden passages, and interactive mechanisms.
- Critical Hit captive-ball target used during battles and other gameplay features.
- Fizmo's Store, allowing players to purchase equipment and items to improve their characters.
- Tiny's Tavern, featuring a spinner-controlled dice game of chance.
- Hidden Temple shot behind the upper flipper that activates double scoring.
- Mountain Passage up/down ramp and an elevated Bridge ramp connecting sections of the playfield.
- Multiple multiball modes, including Dragon Multiball and Gelatinous Cube Multiball.
- Cooperative gameplay allowing multiple players to share campaign progression during a game.
- Tournament mode that disables saved campaign progression and standardizes random gameplay elements.
- Weekly variations in dungeon layouts, character statistics, treasure contents, and shop inventories.
- More than 100 collectible trinkets providing gameplay enhancements and special abilities.
- Original hand-drawn artwork by Vincent Proce, display animations by Paul Chamnankit, and an orchestral soundtrack composed by Cris Velasco.
- Voice performances by Michael Dorn, Kevin Smith, Luke Gygax, Matthew Mercer, Laura Bailey, Marisha Ray, Gerard Way, Brendon Small, and others.
- Optional interactive Treasure Chest topper featuring an animated Mimic, exclusive Mimic Mania mode, and additional playable character.
- Limited Edition production of 740 numbered machines, featuring exclusive artwork, mirrored backglass, enhanced audio, Speaker Expression Lighting, anti-reflection glass, and factory-installed shaker motor.
fields.machine_comments:
- Dungeons & Dragons: The Tyrant's Eye was officially announced on January 3, 2025, as part of the 50th anniversary celebration of the Dungeons & Dragons tabletop role-playing game, originally published in 1974.
- The game was designed by Brian Eddy, whose previous pinball designs include Medieval Madness (1997), Attack from Mars (1995), Stranger Things (2019), and Venom (2023).
- The game was developed in collaboration with Hasbro and Wizards of the Coast, the companies responsible for the Dungeons & Dragons franchise.
- The Limited Edition production quantity of 740 machines was chosen as a tribute to 1974, the year Dungeons & Dragons was originally published.
- The game's setting is the Forgotten Realms, a fantasy campaign world created by Ed Greenwood and first published by TSR in 1987.
- The primary antagonist, Tiamat, is a five-headed dragon goddess who has appeared throughout the history of Dungeons & Dragons.
- The game incorporates traditional Dungeons & Dragons role-playing elements, including character classes, experience points, dice rolls, ability statistics, armor class, equipment, and branching campaign decisions.
- Stern introduced its PinSave system with Dungeons & Dragons, allowing players to save character levels, equipment, and campaign progress through Insider Connected and continue their adventure on other connected machines.
- The game's campaign features three different endings, each unlocking an additional playable character class.
- Procedurally generated Dungeon Crawl layouts change weekly, along with character statistics, equipment locations, treasure chest contents, and shop inventories.
- Michael Dorn, best known for portraying Worf in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, provides the voice of Rath the Relentless.
- The voice cast includes performers associated with Critical Role, including Matthew Mercer, Laura Bailey, and Marisha Ray.
- Luke Gygax, son of Dungeons & Dragons co-creator Gary Gygax, contributed voice work to the game.
- Gerard Way, lead vocalist of My Chemical Romance and creator of The Umbrella Academy, is among the game's voice performers.
- Original music was composed by Cris Velasco, whose work includes music for God of War, Mass Effect, and other video games.
- The Limited Edition includes exclusive cabinet artwork, a mirrored backglass, Dragon Red powder-coated armor, upgraded audio, and a numbered identification plaque.
- Stern released an interactive Treasure Chest topper featuring a transforming Mimic mechanism, an exclusive Mimic Mania mode, and an additional playable Fighter character voiced by Brendon Small.
- The game features a three-flipper layout, with the upper flipper used to access elevated ramps, loops, and hidden playfield shots.

fields.machine_videomode: Dungeons & Dragons: The Tyrant's Eye features Dungeon Crawl, a hybrid video and physical playfield mode. Players navigate procedurally generated, five-level dungeons displayed on the LCD, choosing paths to discover treasure, battle monsters, and avoid traps. Dungeon layouts and rewards change weekly, encouraging exploration and repeated play. The mode incorporates physical pinball shots and, on Premium and Limited Edition models, a mechanically rising dungeon entrance that captures the ball. The game also features animated character battles, dice rolls, story sequences, and campaign decisions displayed on the LCD.

    - Changed how Dragon Multiball works:

              starts at 3 Million and climbs to 8 Million at level ten.

              6 hits on the dragon for each Super Jackpot at level 8 and

                 one is not killed first.

                 that first. Then your attacks will do damage to him.

                 a firebolt from his gauntlet.

         shoot them to heal your party.

             will be attacked.
           - Next, making your way to the dungeons of the castle, you need to
             defeat some guards that are guarding the king.

             attacked by Animated Armor. The Purple shot Dispel Magic one of
             them and will instantly kill one.
           - Next you will face a Shield Guardian. If you shoot the white shots
             you will stealthily get past the Guardian. Or you can fight him.
           - Next you face Helmed Horrors. 
           - Next you have to face two Skeleton Minotaurs before facing Balinor
             himself. A Skeleton will reconstitute when one it is killed if the
             2nd one is not killed first.
           - If Balinor has the Lifeblood Armor, You will have to destroy
             that first. Then your attacks will do damage to him. Every few
             seconds that Balinor is not attacked he will launch a firebolt
             from his gauntlet.
       - When you are between levels and there are green shots lit you can
         shoot them to heal your party.

Update instructions - Games connected to Stern Insider Connected:
1 - Open the coin door and press the black/enter button to enter Test Mode.
2 - Using the 4 buttons on the coin door, navigate to the Stern Insider Connected Setup menu.
3 - Using the 4 buttons on the coin door, navigate down to the Software Update menu.
4 - If a software update is available, this page will give you the option to
    download and install it manually.  From this menu you can also select to install these
    updates automatically.

Update instructions - All Games:
1 - Download the zip file
2 - Unzip the file, this will create a folder that contains SPK file(s).
3 - Open the folder, copy the file(s) to the root level of a FAT32 formatted
    USB stick.  (Do not copy the folder.)
4 - Power game off
5 - Insert USB stick
6 - Turn on game
7 - After game boots up it will give the option for software update
8 - Volume buttons change options for full or quick update. Enter selects the
    option and starts the update.
9 - Once update is completed game will prompt user to power game off and
    remove USB stick.

Update instructions - Games connected to Stern Insider Connected:
1 - Open the coin door and press the black/enter button to enter Test Mode.
2 - Using the 4 buttons on the coin door, navigate to the Stern Insider Connected Setup menu.
3 - Using the 4 buttons on the coin door, navigate down to the Software Update menu.
4 - If a software update is available, this page will give you the option to
    download and install it manually.  From this menu you can also select to install these
    updates automatically.

Update instructions - All Games:
1 - Download the zip file
2 - Unzip the file, this will create a folder that contains SPK file(s).
3 - Open the folder, copy the file(s) to the root level of a FAT32 formatted
    USB stick.  (Do not copy the folder.)
4 - Power game off
5 - Insert USB stick
6 - Turn on game
7 - After game boots up it will give the option for software update
8 - Volume buttons change options for full or quick update. Enter selects the
    option and starts the update.
9 - Once update is completed game will prompt user to power game off and
    remove USB stick.

Update instructions - Games connected to Stern Insider Connected:
1 - Open the coin door and press the black/enter button to enter Test Mode.
2 - Using the 4 buttons on the coin door, navigate to the Stern Insider Connected Setup menu.
3 - Using the 4 buttons on the coin door, navigate down to the Software Update menu.
4 - If a software update is available, this page will give you the option to
    download and install it manually.  From this menu you can also select to install these
    updates automatically.

Update instructions - All Games:
1 - Download the zip file
2 - Unzip the file, this will create a folder that contains SPK file(s).
3 - Open the folder, copy the file(s) to the root level of a FAT32 formatted
    USB stick.  (Do not copy the folder.)
4 - Power game off
5 - Insert USB stick
6 - Turn on game
7 - After game boots up it will give the option for software update
8 - Volume buttons change options for full or quick update. Enter selects the
    option and starts the update.
9 - Once update is completed game will prompt user to power game off and
    remove USB stick.

          - Short ball save for the 3rd and 4th Jackpots collected.

          - Ends when you run out of flips or Find Ann.

               left.
       - Single Ball, Timed Modifier
          - Ends when you drain, run out of time, or Find Ann.

          - Each Jackpot collected adds 25 seconds.
          - Collecting all 6 Jackopts will Find Ann and award a Finishing Bonus based on
